subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in public timeout plus generic queue callback as the supported boundary for abandoning non-cooperative deferred context-engine maintenance?
rationale: Source review can establish that the patch is internally consistent, but it cannot decide whether a new permanent config/API surface and continued execution of an abandoned plugin promise are the intended product and plugin-contract semantics.

options.title: Approve the opt-in boundary
options.body: Accept the disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue hook, and host-side fencing as the supported operator escape hatch for wedged maintenance.

options.title: Reuse the compaction safety budget
options.body: Replace the new setting with the existing host timeout policy, reducing configuration surface but coupling maintenance and compaction budgets and potentially changing upgrades by default.

options.title: Require cooperative cancellation first
options.body: Pause this PR and define an abort-capable context-engine maintenance contract before releasing the lane, accepting a larger plugin API and compatibility project.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue hook, and host-side fencing as the supported operator escape hatch for wedged maintenance.

likelyOwner.reason: The history connects this person to the context-engine API, the merged background-maintenance lifecycle, and adjacent timeout-budget design.
